absent: Locking, sleep and interrupt-context rules for compat cache, trap, SDEI and ftrace paths.
Full layouts of register context, thread state, stacks and flag bit assignments.
Compat call number values, reserved range limit and syscall table contents.
Hardware cache maintenance, TLBI workaround and branch hardening mechanisms.
Exception syndrome encodings, fault address handling and signal delivery details.
SDEI firmware interface, event registration and clobbered register set beyond count.
Ftrace register block offsets, operation structure and direct-call setup.
Software PAN address-space identifier values and errata workaround actions.

findings.text: 64-bit EL0 synchronous fault entry decodes the exception syndrome class and delegates to a dedicated handler family covering calls, memory faults, vector extensions, system traps, alignment, undefined, control-flow integrity, memory operations, guarded stack, debug events, breakpoints and pointer authentication, with a fallback for unknown classes.

32-bit EL0 synchronous entry provides a reduced dispatch tailored to compat execution, including compat system calls, memory faults, vector handling, alignment, undefined and coprocessor traps, emulated coprocessor access, debug events and 32-bit breakpoints, plus a catch-all for other classes.

EL0 asynchronous entries share common wrappers that mark transition from user context, establish appropriate interrupt masking, apply branch hardening for kernel addresses on interrupts, hold RCU or non-maskable protection while invoking the architectural handler, then return to user context; the error path additionally captures syndrome state.

Low-level vector table defines sixteen entry slots spanning privileged thread and handler states and both user execution widths, each offering synchronous, interrupt, fast interrupt and error vectors.

Compat private call handler supports cache maintenance over a user range and installation of a user thread register value with ordering protection and system register update; selectors within the reserved private range but without implementation report not-implemented, while others trigger an illegal-instruction fault with program counter adjusted for execution width.
Compat cache request is rejected for inverted range or nonzero flags and for spans not accessible to user mode before any hardware maintenance is attempted.

Compat cache maintenance proceeds incrementally over bounded chunks of the requested span, abandoning promptly when a fatal signal is present, issuing inner-shareable invalidation where a hardware workaround capability is active, invoking user-safe clean and invalidate per chunk and yielding the processor between chunks until completion or first failure.

User cache clean and invalidate temporarily enables user address access for the maintenance operation, reports a memory fault if the access fails, and always restores protection before returning a status.

Direct call invocation forwards the saved register context to the target function, work detection inspects thread flag state for pending syscall work, and compat dispatch selects the compat table entry using the designated argument register bounded by the compat count.
Compat call entry from user mode combines user-mode entry bookkeeping, a model-specific erratum mitigation, interrupt mask restoration and compat dispatch with matching exit bookkeeping.
Pointer authentication faults from EL0 are converted into illegal-instruction signal delivery carrying fault address and syndrome information.

EL0 coprocessor emulation first validates execution condition using syndrome state or current IT bits, selects a width-specific registration table based on exception class, scans registrations by masked syndrome comparison and invokes the first match, otherwise falls back to undefined-instruction handling; progress advances past the faulting instruction when the condition fails.
Each coprocessor registration associates a mask and expected syndrome value with a handler pointer, and the table ends with an entry lacking a handler that terminates the linear scan.

Detection of exhausted stack for exception handling captures syndrome and fault address, enters non-maskable context, reports task, interrupt and overflow stack extents plus saved registers, then raises a non-maskable panic and parks the CPU without returning; the low-level stub preserves general state onto the overflow stack before entering the C handler.

SDEI entry normalizes privileged access protection according to hardware support before guarding event processing with non-maskable context; event delivery recovers registers clobbered by firmware, runs the registered handler, warns if a synchronous fault altered the saved return location, and then either completes in place for masked kernel context or resumes through a mode-specific vector offset.
Resume displacements from the vector base are 640 for kernel thread context, 1152 for 64-bit user context and 1664 for 32-bit user context.

Function tracer entry preserves caller argument state and frame linkage while building records for the call site and the tracer, invokes the configured tracer with call-site location, caller location and register context, then restores argument state and frame before resuming at the saved return location.

Ops-based tracing locates the operation structure from the return address alignment and may transfer directly to an associated trampoline either immediately or after other tracers; graph and return trampolines capture return-value state and frame information to allow a helper to substitute the original return address.
Default tracer placeholders for classic entry, graph entry and direct trampoline return without effect when no tracer is installed.

Software privileged-access emulation tracks user-access state in the saved status and address-space identifier, disabling user access on kernel entry unless already disabled and re-enabling on exit according to saved state, clearing the emulated bit for older processors; user return always re-enables and applies post-update errata mitigation.
Return to privileged context exits immediately, while return to user context re-examines single-step state and optionally erases task stack contents before exiting.

Several EL0 fault wrappers for pointer authentication, coprocessor and 32-bit breakpoint share entry from user mode, restoration of process interrupt mask, invocation of a C handler and exit to user mode.
